verdicts.issue: N. Madhava Rao was a replacement (for B.L. Mitter, who resigned), not one of the seven original members. The question lists him alongside originals as if interchangeable. fix.question: Connect: B.R. Ambedkar in the chair; K.M. Munshi; Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar; N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar; T.T. Krishnamachari (a later addition). Which committee?
fix.explanation: The seven-member Drafting Committee that drafted the Indian Constitution, chaired by Ambedkar. Originals also included Saiyid Mohammad Saadulla, B.L. Mitter and D.P. Khaitan; Mitter and Khaitan were later replaced by N. Madhava Rao and T.T. Krishnamachari.

verdicts.issue: The Junagadh plebiscite was held on 20 February 1948, not 1947. The Nawab fled in 1947, and the plebiscite (which the cue is the date for) was 1948.

fix.question: Connect: Operation Polo in September 1948 brought one in; a February 1948 plebiscite settled another after the Nawab had fled to Karachi; the Maharaja signed the Instrument on October 26, 1947 for a third. What process?
fix.explanation: Hyderabad (Operation Polo, Sept 13-18 1948), Junagadh (Nawab fled 1947, plebiscite Feb 1948), J&K (Maharaja Hari Singh's accession, 26 Oct 1947) - Patel and V.P. Menon's project.

verdicts.issue: Nehru's actual phrase was 'New Temple of Resurgent India' (per Wikipedia's Bhakra article) — though 'temples of modern India' is the more famous general phrase he applied to dams and steel plants collectively. fix.question: Connect: Nehru's 'temple of modern India' on the Sutlej; the Mahanadi project that became the world's longest earthen dam; one on the Narmada that displaced many. What are these?
fix.explanation: Bhakra Nangal (Sutlej, dedicated 1963), Hirakud (Mahanadi, Odisha), Sardar Sarovar (Narmada, Gujarat, inaugurated 2017). Nehru famously called such dams and steel plants the 'temples of modern India'.
